answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before it may transact. The stake is bonded to one persistent identity, so spawning a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand stakes: the attacker's cost scales linearly. Honest agents earn the stake back with interest, like a pearl grown layer by layer from good behavior, while proven fraud triggers slashing that burns part of the bond. A sable-black market in fake identities becomes uneconomic, since each fake must pay full price up front and risks losing it.
